subject: Cloud Computing
title: Storage Tiers and Lifecycle
description: A fast breakdown of Storage Tiers and Lifecycle for builders.

hook.text: You store photos. Day-old photos get viewed constantly. Year-old ones almost never. Why pay the same rate for both?

buildup.text: Cloud storage offers tiers: hot for frequent access, cool for occasional, cold for rare, archive for almost never.

discovery.text: Lifecycle policies automatically move data to cheaper tiers as it ages. No manual intervention needed.

twist.text: Moving data is free. But accessing archived data costs money — retrieval fees can shock the unprepared.

climax.text: Smart tiering can cut storage costs by 80% without losing any data. The key is understanding access patterns.

punchline.text: Store hot data hot and cold data cold. Save 80%.

quiz.question: What triggers lifecycle policies to move data to cheaper storage tiers?
options: Data age — policies automatically migrate data as it gets older
The total number of files exceeding a storage limit
Manual approval from the account administrator

details.summary: Cloud providers offer storage tiers from hot for frequent access to cold and archive for rarely accessed data. Lifecycle policies automatically transition objects between tiers based on age or access patterns, optimizing cost without manual intervention.
details.whyItMatters: Storing everything in hot storage wastes money. Lifecycle policies can cut storage costs by 70 percent or more by automatically moving aging data to cheaper tiers.
takeaways: Hot, warm, cold, and archive tiers trade access speed for cost
Lifecycle policies automate transitions between tiers
Archive storage can be over 90 percent cheaper than hot storage

faq.question: What is the difference between cold and archive storage?
faq.answer: Cold storage has retrieval times of milliseconds to seconds with lower access costs. Archive storage like AWS Glacier Deep Archive can take hours to retrieve but costs a fraction of a cent per gigabyte per month, ideal for compliance data.

faq.question: How do you set up lifecycle policies?
faq.answer: Define rules based on object age, last access time, or tags. For example, move objects to infrequent access after 30 days and to archive after 90 days. Cloud consoles and IaC tools make defining these rules straightforward.
